_activity: Write the explanation: the three-fifths clause
_licence: ORIGINAL, built on the 11.2 casefile documents (numbered per the signed 11.2 map). Quotes are the casefile's adapted text.
source_document: Document 14 — the Constitution, Article I, 1787 (11.2 Casefile B)
source_text: Section 2. The House of Representatives shall be made up of members chosen every second year by the people. Representatives shall be divided among the states according to their numbers — adding to the whole number of free persons three fifths of all other persons.
prompt: Explain why the three-fifths clause matters. Use the frame.
checklist: Did you say what it means?
model_response: The Constitution counted three of every five enslaved people toward a state's seats in the House, because Southern delegates wanted more power in Congress, which means slaveholding states gained power from people who could not vote and could use it to protect slavery.
